Bayesian epistemology sees belief as a continuous phenomenon coming in degrees called credences.
The Lockean thesis defines belief as credence above a certain threshold.
Bayesian epistemology is based on axioms of probability and the principal principle as static constraints.
The principle of conditionalization governs dynamic constraints on how agents update beliefs upon receiving evidence.

statement: Formal epistemologists aim to replace the bivalent notion of belief with the probabilistic notion of credence.
